newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX stoutly resists Wall Street drag.
newsitem.headline: German DAX stoutly resists Wall Street drag.

text.p: Continued ample liquidity buoyed German shares around record highs on Thursday as the market resisted a pull from Wall Street's overnight decline to continue to forge ahead.

The German DAX, playing catch-up with gains late on Wednesday during the electronic post-bourse session, was trading up 20.88 points at 3,819.39 points in early floor trade, and looked set for a record closing level.
Prices on the day were flat, with the IBIS DAX of electronic trade up 1.40 at 3,820.92, having dropped from a new all-time high of 3,863.91 hit in early trade.
Profit-taking on bank shares, the hot favourites of the past two days, were dragging the market.
Deutsche Bank AG was down 90 pfennigs at 103.40 marks.

Leading the advance was industrial giant and DAX index heavyweight Daimler-Benz AG, which was trading up 5.90 marks or more than four percent at 142.90 marks after announcing plans to sell its stake in computer unit Cap Gemini.

The move was viewed as a strategic plus for Daimler, which has shed many non-core businesses in a bid to boost its profitability. Analysts also welcomed news that the company appears to remain keen on the information technology segment.

Shares in Deutsche Telekom were down 30 pfennigs at 42.60 marks as the market reacted with broad indifference to news that a deal had been reached with the government to transfer Telekom shares to a state development agency.
The deal was in line with expectations, dealers said.
